descriptionChirho: Describing a person who exercises wise caution, forethought, and practical intelligence — a positive quality commended in Proverbs. Arabic 'ذَكِيٌّ' (dhakiyy, intelligent), Korean '슬기롭다/슬기로운' (seulgiropda, wise), Swahili 'mwenye busara' (possessor of wisdom), Hindi 'चतुर' (catur, clever), Spanish 'prudente' all point to an approving sense of discernment and sagacity used across eight occurrences in wisdom literature.

Describing a person who uses cleverness deceptively or manipulatively — a negative quality associated with the serpent (Gen 3:1) and the wicked in Job. Arabic 'الْمُحْتَالِينَ/الماكِرينَ' (al-muḥtālīn/al-mākirīn, schemers/cunning ones) and 'مَاكِرَةً' (mākiratan, deceitful), Korean '간교한' (gangyohan, crafty/sly), Swahili 'werevu/mjanja' (shrewd/sly), Spanish 'astutos/astuta' all confirm the pejorative connotation of trickery and guile across three occurrences.
